title: two baskets with duplicates and a NULL, combined six ways

steps.sql: SELECT item FROM ada ORDER BY item NULLS LAST
SELECT item FROM sean ORDER BY item NULLS LAST
SELECT item FROM ada UNION SELECT item FROM sean ORDER BY item NULLS LAST
steps.note: UNION: every distinct item from either basket, once. the two NULLs count as the same item.

steps.sql: SELECT item FROM ada UNION ALL SELECT item FROM sean ORDER BY item NULLS LAST
steps.note: UNION ALL: both baskets poured into one, nothing removed. 5 + 4 = 9 rows.

steps.sql: SELECT item FROM ada INTERSECT SELECT item FROM sean ORDER BY item NULLS LAST
steps.note: INTERSECT: the distinct items in both baskets: kettle, and NULL, which set operations treat as equal to NULL.

steps.sql: SELECT item FROM ada INTERSECT ALL SELECT item FROM sean ORDER BY item NULLS LAST
steps.note: INTERSECT ALL: as many copies as both baskets have: Ada has 3 kettles, Sean 2, so 2 come out.

steps.sql: SELECT item FROM ada EXCEPT SELECT item FROM sean ORDER BY item NULLS LAST
steps.note: EXCEPT: distinct items in Ada's basket and not in Sean's. only the whisk.

steps.sql: SELECT item FROM ada EXCEPT ALL SELECT item FROM sean ORDER BY item NULLS LAST
steps.note: EXCEPT ALL: each of Sean's copies cancels one of Ada's. 3 kettles minus 2 leaves 1, and the whisk.
